S1.label: bug
S1.suggestionContent:
WHAT: `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` is dereferenced without optional chaining after destructuring `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []`.
WHY: The previous code was `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"`, which was null-safe; now when `destinationCalendar` is null/empty (e.g. handleNewBooking.ts:1063-1067 sets it to `null` when neither eventType nor organizer has one) and `evt.location === MeetLocationType`, destructuring yields `undefined` and `.integration` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined`, crashing the booking creation flow.
HOW: Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"`.

S2.label: bug
S2.suggestionContent:
WHAT: The fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` only executes when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so it compares `cal.externalId` against `null`/`undefined` and matches nothing (the same wrong pattern is duplicated in deleteEvent at lines 315-317).
WHY: When `updateEvent`/`deleteEvent` are called without an externalCalendarId, `selectedCalendar`/`calendarId` now resolves to `undefined` instead of the host's destination calendar externalId (old code fell back to `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`), so the Google API is invoked with an undefined calendarId and the update/delete targets the wrong (or default) calendar or errors.
HOW: Find the destination calendar for the current credential (e.g. by credentialId) rather than comparing `externalId` to the already-falsy `externalCalendarId`, or restore the single fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.externalId`.

S3.label: bug
S3.suggestionContent:
WHAT: `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` silently does nothing when `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`.
WHY: For a COLLECTIVE event where neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists, the evt field is set to `null` (lines 1063-1067), so the collected `teamDestinationCalendars` of the other hosts are dropped and those hosts are never invited — defeating the multi-host support this PR adds.
HOW: Initialize to an array (e.g. `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` before pushing, or default the field to `[]` instead of `null`) so team destination calendars are always appended.

S4.label: bug
S4.suggestionContent:
WHAT: `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined` drops the previous non-calendar fallback `result.credentialId`.
WHY: For non-calendar results (video events) `referencesToCreate` now stores `credentialId: undefined` where it previously stored `result.credentialId`, so the persisted video reference loses its credentialId; later code that looks the reference up by credentialId (e.g. handleCancelBooking.ts:491-502 deleting the video meeting, or EventManager.updateLocation) can no longer resolve the credential and the meeting is not cleaned up.
HOW: Keep the fallback for non-calendar results: `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : result.credentialId` (i.e. just `result.credentialId` for both branches).

S5.label: performance
S5.suggestionContent:
WHAT: The new `for (const destination of event.destinationCalendar)` loop performs a `prisma.credential.findUnique` on every destination whose credential is not found in the cached `this.calendarCredentials` (line 344); the same per-reference DB lookup was added in updateAllCalendarEvents at line 517.
WHY: For collective bookings with multiple hosts this turns one in-memory lookup into up to N sequential database round-trips added to the booking-creation hot path, scaling with host count.
HOW: Resolve all missing credential ids in a single batched query (`prisma.credential.findMany({ where: { id: { in: missingIds } } })`) before the loop and build a lookup map.

S6.label: bug
S6.suggestionContent: `mainHostDestinationCalendar` can be `undefined` because `evt.destinationCalendar` may now be null or an empty array (callers such as handleNewBooking pass `: null` / `: []`). The old code used `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`, but the new line dereferences `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining, throwing `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')` whenever `evt.location === MeetLocationType`. Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"` to preserve the null-safe fallback.

S7.label: bug
S7.suggestionContent: The Meet-location fallback destructures `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` and then reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining. When `destinationCalendar` is an empty array (which this PR now produces in many callers, e.g. handleCancelBooking.ts, the payment webhooks, confirm/editLocation/deleteCredential/requestReschedule handlers all set `[]` when there is no destination calendar), the destructured value is `undefined` and `.integration` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')`, aborting event creation. Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration` to preserve the previous optional-chained behavior.

S8.label: bug
S8.suggestionContent: handleNewBooking.ts (lines 1063-1067) can produce `destinationCalendar: null` (and other callers pass `[]`), but here `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` yields `undefined` for both, and line 119 then reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining, throwing `TypeError` on every booking without a destination calendar. The previous code used `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`, which was null-safe; guard it (e.g. `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"`) so the Google-Meet fallback does not crash.

S9.label: bug
S9.suggestionContent: Dead computation in the fallback: the else branch runs only when externalCalendarId is falsy, yet it calls `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)`, comparing every cal.externalId to undefined. Nothing can match, so selectedCalendar is always undefined and the fallback that previously returned `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` is lost. Match the intended criterion (destination calendar's own externalId/credentialId), not the already-falsy externalCalendarId.

S10.label: bug
S10.suggestionContent: Same dead-computation defect in deleteEvent: the else branch executes only when externalCalendarId is falsy, yet the predicate `(cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` compares against undefined and can never match, so calendarId falls through to "primary" and the event is deleted from the wrong calendar instead of the booking's destination calendar. Fix the predicate to use the destination calendar's externalId (or credentialId) rather than the falsy externalCalendarId.

S11.label: bug
S11.suggestionContent: Destructuring `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` yields undefined when destinationCalendar is an empty array (which this PR now produces in many callers, e.g. handleCancelBooking:255, webhook:119, paypal-webhook:156, confirm.handler:179). The subsequent `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar"` then throws TypeError, aborting event creation whenever location is Google Meet and destinationCalendar is empty. Guard the access: `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"`.

S12.label: bug
S12.suggestionContent: In updateEvent (and the identical pattern at lines 315-317 in deleteEvent), the fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` compares each element's externalId to the same `externalCalendarId` the ternary already found falsy, so it can never match and always returns undefined. The intended fallback to the destination calendar's externalId is lost, sending the update/delete to the wrong calendar ("primary"). Select the relevant destination calendar by credential instead, as done in createEvent.

S13.label: bug
S13.suggestionContent: The comment still describes a graceful fallback ("as a fallback we will only check the first one"), but the code no longer guards the absent case: `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is the first element of `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` and is `undefined` when the event has no destination calendar, so `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` throws a TypeError before the Cal Video fallback can run. The previous `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration` was safe and let the fallback apply. Either restore optional chaining (`mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`) so the comment holds, or update the comment to state that a missing destination calendar is not handled.

S1.label: bug
S1.suggestionContent: WHAT: isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed with && instead of ||. WHY: isTeamAdmin returns truthy for role ADMIN or OWNER while isTeamOwner returns true only for OWNER, so the && expression is only true for OWNERs; team ADMINs are treated as unauthorized and get FORBIDDEN when adding guests, contradicting the variable's intent. HOW: use `(await isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)) || (await isTeamOwner(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0))`.

S2.label: security
S2.suggestionContent: WHAT: The blacklist is compared case-sensitively against guest input while blacklistedGuestEmails are lowercased. WHY: blacklistedGuestEmails entries are lowercased but the filter compares `guest` verbatim (`!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`); an authenticated user can add a blacklisted address simply by changing its case (e.g. `Foo@bar.com` vs `foo@bar.com`), bypassing the configured BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restriction. HOW: normalize the guest before comparison, e.g. `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest.toLowerCase())`.

S3.label: bug
S3.suggestionContent: WHAT: sendAddGuestsEmails is called with the raw `guests` input instead of the filtered `uniqueGuests`. WHY: any submitted email that was already an attendee (or is blacklisted) is dropped by uniqueGuests for the DB write but still appears in the `guests` array, so in email-manager.ts the `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` branch marks that existing attendee as a new guest and sends them a full AttendeeScheduledEmail re-confirmation instead of the add-guests notification. HOW: pass `uniqueGuests` (or the newly-created attendee emails) to sendAddGuestsEmails.

S4.label: security
S4.suggestionContent: Case-sensitivity bypass of the guest blacklist. `blacklistedGuestEmails` is lowercased on the list side (line 71) but the input side is compared raw: `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` (line 77). A guest email submitted with any different casing (e.g. `Foo@Bar.com` when the blacklist holds `foo@bar.com`) passes the filter and is persisted, defeating BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS. Normalize the input before comparison, e.g. filter on `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest.toLowerCase())` (and likewise lowercase `guest` for the attendee dedup check).

S5.label: security
S5.suggestionContent: Inconsistent email normalization for identity checks. Both the authorization check `attendee.email === user.email` (line 52) and the existing-attendee dedup `guest === attendee.email` (line 76) use strict case-sensitive equality, while emails are treated as case-insensitive everywhere else in this handler (the blacklist block directly below lowercases). Consequence: a legitimate attendee whose stored casing differs from their session email is wrongly FORBIDDEN, and a guest differing from an existing attendee only by case is duplicated rather than filtered. Compare on a normalized form (both sides `.toLowerCase()`), consistent with the blacklist normalization.

S6.label: bug
S6.suggestionContent: Case-sensitive identity comparison misroutes emails. `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` compares the freshly-added guest list against stored attendee emails with strict case-sensitive matching. A newly added guest whose casing differs from the stored value falls into the `else` branch and receives the AttendeeAddGuestsEmail template intended for pre-existing attendees, while existing attendees can receive the wrong one. Normalize both sides (e.g. compare `attendee.email.toLowerCase()` against a lowercased newGuests set).

S7.label: bug
S7.suggestionContent: The flag is named `isTeamAdminOrOwner` but is computed with `&&` (both admin AND owner). A team admin who is not the owner, or the owner who is not flagged admin, will fail this check, so the guard at line 54 wrongly throws FORBIDDEN for legitimate admins/owners. Use `||` between isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner.

S8.label: bug
S8.suggestionContent: `uniqueGuests` is computed (line 74) to exclude already-invited and blacklisted emails and is the value actually inserted into the booking, but `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` is called with the raw input `guests`. The untransformed value is used where the filtered one was intended, so the email-manager's `newGuests.includes(...)` classification operates on the wrong list; pass `uniqueGuests`.

S9.label: bug
S9.suggestionContent: The variable `isTeamAdminOrOwner` names an OR condition, but the code combines `isTeamAdmin(...)` and `isTeamOwner(...)` with `&&`, so it is true only when the user is both admin AND owner. Either the name is wrong or the operator is; as written the permission check at line 54 denies a plain team admin, contradicting what the identifier promises. Use `||` to match the name (or rename if AND is intended).

S10.label: bug
S10.suggestionContent: `Tooltip content="Remove email"` is a hard-coded English user-facing string, while the surrounding code in this same component routes user text through `t()` (e.g. `t("add_another")` on line 69). This string bypasses the translation mechanism and will never be localised; it should use a translation key.

S11.label: bug
S11.suggestionContent: In `onError`, `message` is always a non-empty template string (`"${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}"`), so the fallback `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` is unreachable and the newly added `unable_to_add_guests` translation is never shown. The user is instead shown a raw error code prefix like `BAD_REQUEST: ...` rather than the translated message; the fallback and code prefix handling should be corrected so the intended translated text reaches the user.

S12.label: bug
S12.suggestionContent: The callee `sendAddGuestsEmails(calEvent, newGuests)` expects the array of *new* guests: it uses `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` to send AttendeeScheduledEmail (a fresh invitation) to new guests and AttendeeAddGuestsEmail (notification) to everyone else. The caller passes `guests` — the raw input — instead of the deduplicated `uniqueGuests` computed at lines 74-90. Any email in `guests` that was filtered out as already-an-attendee (or blacklisted) is therefore treated as a new guest, causing that existing attendee to be re-sent a full invitation. Pass `uniqueGuests` here.

S13.label: bug
S13.suggestionContent: The handler passes the raw input `guests` to `sendAddGuestsEmails`, but the email manager's `newGuests` parameter is documented/used as the set of guests that were actually added (`newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` selects who gets the full `AttendeeScheduledEmail`). Since the handler filters the added guests into `uniqueGuests` (dropping addresses that already belong to an attendee or are blacklisted) before creating attendees, any submitted address that was not actually added is still treated as a new guest here — an existing attendee re-submitted by the requester receives a duplicate booking-confirmation email with a new ICS REQUEST. Pass `uniqueGuests` instead of `guests`.

S14.label: bug
S14.suggestionContent: The handler never deduplicates within the incoming `guests` array. `uniqueGuests` only excludes emails that are already attendees or blacklisted, so a request containing the same email twice (or two equivalent emails) yields two identical `guestsFullDetails` entries. Since the wire schema `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` has no uniqueness refine (the uniqueness check lives only in the client's AddGuestsDialog), the server cannot rely on the UI: either duplicate attendee rows are persisted (state corruption of the booking's attendee list) or, if a DB unique constraint on (bookingId,email) exists, `createMany` throws an unhandled Prisma error. Deduplicate the input server-side (e.g. `[...new Set(guests)]`) and/or add the uniqueness refinement to `ZAddGuestsInputSchema`.

S15.label: bug
S15.suggestionContent: Check-then-insert race: the handler reads `booking.attendees` at the start, filters against it, then inserts in a separate `prisma.booking.update ... createMany` with no transaction or unique guard. Two concurrent addGuests calls for the same guest both see it as absent and both insert, producing duplicate attendees. Wrap the read+filter+insert in a transaction (or rely on a unique constraint on (bookingId, email) and handle the conflict) so concurrent requests cannot both succeed.

S16.label: bug
S16.suggestionContent: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is built with `&&`, so it is true only when the caller is BOTH a team admin AND the team owner — it should be `||`. As written, a team admin who is not the owner (and vice versa) evaluates to false and is denied by the `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee)` throw at line 54, so admins/owners cannot add guests to team bookings. Replace `&&` with `||` between the `isTeamAdmin` and `isTeamOwner` calls.

S17.label: Functional concern outside assigned data exposure class
S17.suggestionContent: Using `guests` instead of `uniqueGuests` when sending emails

S18.label: Permission concern outside assigned data exposure class

S1.label: bug
S1.suggestionContent:
WHAT: The 3rd argument to `refreshOAuthTokens` is `credentialId` (= `credential.id`, line 53), but the function's parameter is `userId` (`refreshOAuthTokens(refreshFunction, appSlug, userId)`).
WHY: When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED, the sync endpoint is sent `calcomUserId: <credential id>` instead of the user id, so Bigin credentials are synced against the wrong/non-existent user (all other apps correctly pass `credential.userId`).
HOW: Pass `credential.userId` instead of `credentialId` as the third argument.

S2.label: bug
S2.suggestionContent:
WHAT: `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema)` assigns the zod `safeParse` result object `{ success, data }` (see parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:29), not the parsed credential data, and this wrapper is persisted directly as `credential.key`.
WHY: The stored key no longer matches `googleCredentialSchema`, so the next time the credential is loaded `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` (line 75) throws and Google Calendar is broken until the credential is re-created. Every other caller (office365/zoom/salesforce) unwraps `.data`; only google stores the raw return value.
HOW: Use `parseRefreshTokenResponse(...).data` (or restore `googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)`) when writing the key.

S3.label: bug
S3.suggestionContent:
WHAT: In the credential-sharing branch `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the raw `fetch` `Response` object instead of a parsed token payload, yet several callers treat the result as an already-parsed token object.
WHY: Callers such as hubspot (`hubspotRefreshToken.expiresIn`), zoho-bigin (`tokenInfo.data.error`), zohocrm (`zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error`) and googlecalendar (`res?.data`) read `.data`/token fields off the return value; a `Response` has neither, so the sync path yields `undefined`/`NaN` or throws a TypeError — the feature's primary code path is broken for those apps.
HOW: Parse the response (e.g. `const data = await response.json(); return data;`) before returning, or make every caller await the appropriate response handler.

S4.label: bug
S4.suggestionContent:
WHAT: The new block fetches and persists a fresh access token (`accessTokenParsed.data`) but then creates the `jsforce.Connection` with the stale `credentialKey.access_token` (line 106) instead of the just-refreshed token.
WHY: The refreshed token is written to the DB but never used for the connection; if the old token was expired, jsforce must refresh again (extra round trip) or fail, and the DB/connection state diverge.
HOW: Pass the new access token (`accessTokenParsed.data.access_token`) to the `jsforce.Connection`.

S5.label: security
S5.suggestionContent: The webhook secret is compared with the `!==` operator, which short-circuits on the first differing byte and leaks the secret via response timing (timing attack). An attacker can iteratively recover CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET and then forge requests that create/update arbitrary user credential keys (decrypted with the AES key) via this endpoint. Use a constant-time comparison, e.g. crypto.timingSafeEqual on equal-length buffers, guarding for length mismatch first.

S6.label: bug
S6.suggestionContent: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the SafeParseReturnType wrapper (`{ success, data }`), not the parsed value the old `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)` returned. Assigning it to `key` and persisting `data: { key }` stores the wrapper as the credential key; the next read does `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` and throws, making the credential unusable. Use the `.data` result.

S7.label: bug
S7.suggestionContent: In sharing mode refreshOAuthTokens returns the raw fetch Response (no `.data`), but the google caller reads `res?.data` and then `token.access_token`, throwing a TypeError swallowed by the catch, so the token is never refreshed.

S8.label: bug
S8.suggestionContent: refreshOAuthTokens' third parameter is the Cal.com userId (used as `calcomUserId` in the sync request and to decide whether sharing runs), but this call passes `credentialId`. Every other caller passes `credential.userId`, so the credential-sync endpoint receives a credential row id as the user id and shared credentials are fetched/updated for the wrong identity. Pass `credential.userId` here.

S9.label: bug
S9.suggestionContent: refreshOAuthTokens' third parameter is `userId` (declared in refreshOAuthTokens.ts line 3 and used as `calcomUserId: userId.toString()`), but this call passes `credentialId` (the Credential row id, line 53) instead of the user id. When credential sharing is enabled the customer's sync endpoint receives a credential id labelled as calcomUserId and cannot resolve the correct Cal.com user. Pass `credential.userId` (the BiginToken/credential payload carries it) or plumb the user id through refreshAccessToken.

S10.label: bug
S10.suggestionContent: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the whole safeParse result object `{ success, data }` (parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts line 29), not the parsed value. The previous code was `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)`, which returned the token object directly. Other callers (office365calendar, salesforce) read `tokenResponse.success`/`.data`, confirming the wrapper contract. Here the wrapper is stored verbatim as the credential key, so the persisted key becomes `{ success: true, data: {...} }` and is later unparseable by googleCredentialSchema. Use `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(...).data;`.

S11.label: bug
S11.suggestionContent: parseRefreshTokenResponse now returns the whole zod safeParse result ({success, data}), not the parsed credential data (the previous `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)` returned data directly). This caller assigns that wrapper to `key` and persists `data: { key }`, so the stored Google credential becomes `{success:true,data:{...}}` instead of the credentials object, breaking subsequent reads of the key. Unwrap the result, e.g. `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema).data`.

S12.label: bug
S12.suggestionContent: refreshOAuthTokens' third parameter is `userId: number | null` (used as calcomUserId in the credential-sync request), but this call passes `credentialId` (a credential id), unlike every other call site which passes `credential.userId`. The sync endpoint will receive a credential id where a Cal.com user id is expected. Pass `credential.userId`.

S13.label: bug
S13.suggestionContent: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the zod SafeParse result (`{ success, data }`), not the parsed credentials. Assigning it straight to `key` and persisting `data: { key }` stores the wrapper object instead of the credential, corrupting the user's stored key. Use `parseRefreshTokenResponse(...).data` (as office365/salesforce/zoom already do) — or make the helper return the parsed data.

S14.label: bug
S14.suggestionContent: `res?.data` assumes the value returned by refreshOAuthTokens has a `.data` field (true for the `fetchTokens.res` branch), but when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED the helper returns a raw `fetch()` Response, which has no `.data`. Then `token.access_token` throws. Either parse the shared-mode Response here or have refreshOAuthTokens return a normalized `{ data }` shape.

S15.label: bug
S15.suggestionContent: The JSDoc documents two different parameters with the same text: both `@param appData.type` and `@param appData.appId` are described as "the app slug". The body uses `appData.type` as the credential `type` and only `appData.appId` as the app slug, so the `type` doc contradicts the code and misleads callers. Document `type` as the credential type.

S16.label: bug
S16.suggestionContent: The third parameter is named/documented as `userId` (comment: "the credential belongs to a user"), but the new zoho-bigin call site passes `credentialId`, so the request sends `calcomUserId: <credentialId>` — a credential row id where a Cal.com user id is expected. Pass `credential.userId` or rename/document the parameter if a credential id is intended.

S1.label: bug
S1.suggestionContent: WHAT: retryCount is incremented with a read-value computed at the start of the run (`retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1`) instead of an atomic increment. WHY: if two cron invocations overlap (or the same reminder is processed twice before the write commits), both read the same retryCount and both write N+1, so failures are undercounted and the reminder can loop forever without ever reaching the `retryCount > 1` deletion threshold. HOW: use `data: { retryCount: { increment: 1 } }` so the increment is atomic (the initial read value is then irrelevant).

S2.label: bug
S2.suggestionContent: WHAT: the catch block performs an unguarded `prisma.workflowReminder.update` while handling the scheduling error. WHY: if this write itself rejects (e.g. the row was concurrently removed, or a transient DB error), the rejection is not caught and escapes the for-loop, aborting the whole cron run so all remaining reminders go unprocessed. HOW: wrap the retryCount update in its own try/catch (log and continue) so a failure to record the retry does not abort processing of the remaining reminders.

S3.label: performance
S3.suggestionContent: WHAT: the deleteMany WHERE now uses `OR` between `(method = SMS AND scheduledDate <= now)` and `retryCount > 1`, but WorkflowReminder has no index on the newly added retryCount column. WHY: Postgres cannot satisfy a two-way OR using the existing (method, scheduled, scheduledDate) index and will fall back to a sequential scan of the entire WorkflowReminder table on every cron invocation, turning a previously indexed delete into a full table scan as the table grows. HOW: add an index on retryCount (or restructure so each branch is index-usable), then re-check the query plan.

S4.label: bug
S4.suggestionContent: The comment "//delete all scheduled sms reminders where scheduled date is past current date" no longer describes the deleteMany below it. After this change the query also deletes reminders with retryCount > 1, and that OR branch has no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` filter, so non-SMS (email) reminders with retryCount > 1 are now deleted too. Update the comment (or add the missing SMS filter to the retryCount branch) so the prose matches what the code actually deletes.

S5.suggestionContent: The deleteMany OR clause deletes any reminder with retryCount > 1 regardless of method.

S6.suggestionContent: The failed-send branch does not increment retryCount on the success path.

S7.label: bug
S7.suggestionContent: This new `prisma.workflowReminder.update` sits inside the catch block, which is NOT protected by any try/catch. If this update throws (e.g. the reminder was already removed by the `deleteMany` at the top of the file during a concurrent run -> Prisma P2025, or a transient DB error), the exception escapes the `for` loop and rejects the handler, so all remaining unscheduled reminders are skipped and the cron request fails. Previously the catch only did `console.log`, so a single bad reminder never aborted the batch and the endpoint always returned 200. Wrap this update in its own try/catch (or `updateMany`/catch-and-log) so a failed retry-count write cannot take down the whole scheduling run.

S8.label: bug
S8.suggestionContent: The second OR branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` has no `method` filter, unlike the first branch (`method: WorkflowMethods.SMS`). Because `retryCount` is a generic column on WorkflowReminder used by all reminder methods, this deleteMany now permanently deletes every reminder of ANY method (including EMAIL) whose retryCount exceeds 1, even though this cron is only supposed to clean up SMS reminders. Add `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` to this branch (or scope the whole where to SMS) so non-SMS reminders are never destroyed.

S9.label: bug
S9.suggestionContent: `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` is a read-modify-write of the value fetched at the top of the handler, not an atomic increment. Two overlapping cron runs both read the same retryCount and both write the same +1, losing an update, so failed reminders can be retried indefinitely and never reach the `gt: 1` deletion threshold. Use Prisma's atomic `retryCount: { increment: 1 }` instead of computing from the stale in-memory value (same issue in the else branch at lines 179-186).

S10.label: bug
S10.suggestionContent: The deleteMany OR clause with retryCount > 1 is not scoped to SMS.

S11.label: bug
S11.suggestionContent: The retryCount increment is duplicated in the else-branch and catch.

S12.label: bug
